page: Google Cloud Platform a2-ultragpu-8g is an accelerator-optimized virtual machine engineered for distributed deep learning and large-scale artificial intelligence workloads. It integrates eight NVIDIA Ampere A100 GPUs totaling 640 GB of VRAM, supported by a host system running 96 vCPUs (48 physical cores) powered by 2.2 GHz Intel Xeon x86_64 processors. Host memory capacity measures 1360.0 GB (14.17 GB per core), and the platform includes 3216 GB of local NVMe SSD storage across 8 drives. The instance does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate extreme performance in specialized domains paired with trade-offs in general computing. LLM inference benchmarks place the instance in the top 10% across prompt processing and generation for 7B and 70B models, driven by the aggregate GPU memory bandwidth and capacity. On the host CPU, multi-core metrics excel, with stress-ng multi-core computing reaching the top 25% (75780.48) and clang compilation achieving strong throughput. In contrast, single-core CPU metrics fall into the bottom 25%, as seen in stress-ng (1201.29) and Geekbench single-core (1060.0), reflecting the moderate 2.2 GHz base clock frequency.

The dense hardware configuration provides solid cost efficiency for aggregated training pipelines, large-scale inference, and GPU-centric HPC. Because CPU single-thread throughput is restrained, running standard web serving, single-threaded batch data transformations, or sequential tasks represents inefficient resource utilization. Instead, the hardware profile is tailored for large language model deployment, distributed model fine-tuning, complex ray tracing, and high-throughput vector or memory caching operations.
description: Google Cloud Platform a2-ultragpu-8g is an accelerator-optimized instance designed for large-scale AI and deep learning workloads. The system combines eight NVIDIA Ampere A100 GPUs with a combined 640 GB of VRAM, 96 dedicated vCPUs (48 physical cores) based on 2.2 GHz Intel Xeon architecture, 1360.0 GB of system RAM, and 3216 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Benchmark evaluations highlight top-tier performance in large language model inference across 7B and 70B models, alongside top-quartile multi-core CPU and memory bandwidth results. Single-core performance sits in the bottom quartile, indicating that the instance is optimized for massively parallel workloads rather than single-threaded computing. The hardware footprint provides dense computing capability tailored for deep learning training, distributed model serving, and high-performance computing tasks.
